intro: At Ursaworks, our mission is to advance robotics and industry by bringing together students who are passionate about innovation. Our focus is on fostering a collaborative environment where students from any background can develop their skills through competition.
We're committed to nurturing talent and promoting hard work to prepare our members for future challenges in technology. All WashU students are welcome to join and participate!
ourRobot: Each year, the ARC Robotics Competition challenges teams to design and build robots for a combat-style game. Last season, we developed and tested the Infantry, Sentry, and Hero, and this season we're adding an Engineer:

aboutHighlights.name: Learn By Building
aboutHighlights.description: Members design, machine, wire, and program real competition robots from the ground up. Whether you're into mechanical design, embedded systems, or computer vision, you'll ship work that ends up on the field.

aboutHighlights.name: All Majors, All Levels
aboutHighlights.description: No robotics experience required — all WashU students are welcome. Experienced members mentor newcomers, and every subteam has room for people who want to learn.

aboutHighlights.name: Built To Compete
aboutHighlights.description: We put our engineering to the test each season at ARC events across North America, learning from every match and coming back stronger.

arc.title: What Is ARC
description: ARC Robotics — formerly RoboMaster North America — runs an annual competition where university teams from around the world showcase their engineering through tactical combat and technical challenges.
The ARC Championship draws more than 20 international and domestic teams across three events: a 1v1 competition, a 3v3 competition, and an engineering challenge.

robots.name: Infantry
description: The Infantry are the most versatile members of the team, combining mobility, adaptability, and solid firepower.

Their agility allows them to contest map resources, flank opponents, and coordinate attacks alongside the Hero. With skilled drivers, Infantry can shift quickly between offense and defense, making them the backbone of the 3v3 match.

robots.name: Sentry
description: The Sentry uses vision algorithms and onboard processing to track, target, and fire at opponents without a human driver. In the 3v3 format, it provides constant automated pressure and forces enemy robots to adapt their movements.

While it lacks the adaptability of human-driven units, its relentless precision and endurance make it a valuable asset that punishes careless advances and supports teammates through consistent suppression fire.

robots.name: Hero
description: The Hero is the powerhouse of the lineup, armed with heavier weapons that deal more damage per shot than any other unit. Designed to dominate direct confrontations, the Hero often leads offensive maneuvers and forces opponents to respect its presence on the field.
Its higher survivability and firepower make it the focal point of many strategies, with teams relying on it to break stalemates and secure key objectives.

robots.name: Engineer
description: The Engineer trades firepower for dexterity: it carries no launcher, but it is the only robot allowed to handle the Objectives that score Victory Points. Using its arm and claw, it lifts the cube off the Central High Ground, pulls pipes from the central bucket and feeds them through the Pipe Chute, and recovers donuts from the zig-zag poles.

With 600 HP, the most of any robot in the 3v3 lineup, the Engineer is built to keep working under fire while teammates cover it. Its claw is designed to fail safe, springing open on its own if the robot is defeated so it never keeps holding an Objective.
The Engineer is new for the 2026–27 season and still in development. The image shown is an early concept sketch, not the final robot.

competitions.name: ARC Championship (ARCC)
competitions.description: The premier collegiate ARC competition in the region. Top university teams design, build, and battle advanced robots in high-energy, esports-style matches — combining mechanical design, computer vision, embedded systems, and AI on an international stage.

competitions.name: Midwest ARC Regional
competitions.description: A key qualifier and community hub for universities across the central United States. Teams test their robots, refine strategies, and build match experience ahead of the ARC Championship — a showcase of Midwest engineering talent.
